title: Implement a New Performance Logging Level
description: The ProdigiForge Engine's logging system needs to be extended to support a dedicated log level for performance-critical messages. This will help developers profile specific parts of the engine without being flooded by general debug or info messages. The task is broken down into three sessions: defining the new level and its macro, implementing the backend handling, and demonstrating its usage in the main application loop. This requires understanding the existing logging pattern, modifying both header and source files, and retaining context between development sessions.

project_spec.name: ProdigiForge Engine
project_spec.description:
ProdigiForge Engine is an expert-level C game-engine project crafted specifically to accelerate the workflow of game-content creators, level designers, and technical artists.  While it delivers a full real-time 3-D runtime with graphics, physics, audio, AI, networking, and scripting, every subsystem is exposed through an in-process MVVM-driven "live workspace" that lets users iterate on assets, behaviors, and scenes without rebuilding or restarting the application.  The engine’s built-in level editor, task automation scripts, and data-oriented Entity-Component-System make it as much a productivity suite as a run-time, letting multidisciplinary teams create, preview, and optimize content in minutes instead of hours.

At its core, ProdigiForge treats *productivity* as a first-class citizen.  Each feature—resource hot-reloading, command-pattern-based undo/redo, asynchronous asset import, and scriptable build pipelines—feeds into a continuous feedback loop that bridges the gap between editing and play-testing.  The MVVM architecture cleanly separates the simulation (Model), editor/render views (View), and the reactive data-binding layer (ViewModel), enabling deterministic headless builds while still supporting rich in-engine tooling through ImGui overlays.  Combined with Object Pools for memory-safe instancing, a robust State Machine for gameplay flow, and Observer patterns for UI updates, the engine scales seamlessly from solo prototypes to AAA production without sacrificing developer velocity.
dependencies: SDL2 – cross-platform windowing, input_handling, and game_loop timing
cimgui (Dear ImGui C bindings) – immediate-mode GUI used as the View layer
Vulkan SDK (via Volk) – modern graphics_rendering backend
LuaJIT (FFI) – lightning-fast scripting_system and ViewModel data binding
SQLite3 – save_system persistence and asset-catalog indexing
stb_* single-file libs – images, fonts, resource_management helpers
libuv – cross-platform async I/O for hot-reload workflows
zstd – high-speed asset compression and streaming
